turns.text: In two sentences: what's our biggest workforce opportunity right now?

By the widest supply–demand gap, your biggest opportunity right now is Industrial Machinery Mechanics: the Bay Area projects about 550 openings a year against roughly 159 regional completions, a shortfall of 391 — the largest of any occupation in your Advanced Manufacturing sector. Your consortium already supplies about 72 of those completions a year, and the next-widest gap, Machinists, sits at 355.
Good — now the one caveat I most need to know.

The one caveat: that 391 is a regional shortfall, not svamp's alone to fill. It's the Bay Area's roughly 550 openings measured against every Bay-Area college's completions combined — and svamp already supplies about 72 of them — so read 391 as the region's gap, not a target only svamp must close.
And where would I verify it?

Two authorities sit behind it. The demand side is the Centers of Excellence regional occupational projection — 2024 base-year employment projected to 2029; the supply side is CCCCO DataMart program completions, a three-year average through 2024-25. You can corroborate the Industrial Machinery Mechanics row itself on your sector dashboard at preview.kallipolis.us/svamp, on the occupations lens.
